deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a fair-copy set of lecture notes on ancient history, from a chapter on Egypt, 'Zweite Periode: Von der Alleinherrschaft Psammetichs bis auf die persische Eroberung Aegyptens durch Cambyses, 660–525'. The notes follow the style of Heeren-type Göttingen lectures on ancient states. The next page begins chapter 'VII Karthago'. The handwriting and the bundle name (HB.Lagrange1816) suggest these are not Gauss's own notes. They may be student or family notes that ended up bound with Gauss's papers. That is my inference, not certain.

Content of the page, in order:
(1) Neco (Necho II) planned a canal joining the Red Sea to the Mediterranean (the sentence is continued from the previous page) but did not carry it out. He then had Africa circumnavigated. He reigned 16 years.
(2) His son Psammis (Psamtik II) reigned only 6 years. A marginal date 'v. 588' is inserted here. Psammis prepared an expedition (written 'nach Aegypten', historically to Ethiopia/Nubia) but died before it set out.
(3) Apries waged a naval war against the Phoenicians, but Tyre fell to Nebuchadnezzar. Apries campaigned against the Cyreneans and was defeated. This provoked a great revolt in Egypt. He sent his general Amasis to suppress it, but Amasis put himself at the head of the malcontents and became king. Apries died in 563.
(4) Under Amasis, Egypt, previously closed to foreigners, was opened: Nile navigation and foreign access were permitted. The founding of the Persian Empire falls in his reign.
(5) His son Psammenit (Psamtik III, corrected in the manuscript from 'Psammis') reigned only 6 months. Amasis died in 525.

There is no derivation, computation or mathematical problem to reconstruct.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: 'Zuge nach Aegypten' makes no sense for an Egyptian king. Herodotus (II.161) has Psammis' expedition directed against Ethiopia. Either the writer slipped or the word should be read 'Aethiopien'.

The dates follow early-19th-century chronology: Apries † 563 and Amasis † 525, with Psammenit's reign then reaching into 525. Modern dates are Apries deposed c. 570 and Amasis † 526. This is not an error relative to the sources of the time.
Minor grammatical slips in the notes: 'ehe der Zug zu Stande kamen', and 'so viel wie wollten' for 'so viel sie wollten'.

results.what: Historical lecture notes on the Saite dynasty of Egypt (Necho II, Psamtik II, Apries, Amasis, Psamtik III), consistent with Herodotus Book II and Heeren-style lectures on ancient history
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus (source); Göttingen ancient-history lecture tradition (A. H. L. Heeren)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a non-mathematical history notebook entry on ancient Egypt, probably not even in Gauss's hand. It contains nothing of mathematical-historical significance.

checkable.asserts: Length in years of the 'second period' (Psammetich's sole rule to the Persian conquest) given in the chapter heading
Implied span from Apries' death (563) to Amasis' death (525) in the notes' chronology (Amasis' reign counted from Apries' death)

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the manuscript reads 'mitländische' (single t), not 'mittländische'.
Line 3: 'Theil von [?]' is unclear in the image. It appears to be a short word followed by a comma before 'nemlich Afrika umschiffen zu lassen'.
Line 5: the marginal insertion 'v. 588' (in red/brown ink) sits above 'Jahr. Er machte', i.e. it dates the following sentence or the reign change.
Line 6: 'Zuge nach Aegypten' is what the transcription gives. Check against the image: historically expected 'Aethiopien'.
Line 11: 'wodurch er seinen' is doubtful. The image may read 'weswegen' or 'wogegen'.
Line 13: 'Cyrenaeer' has a red-ink correction on the 'r'.
Line 17: 'vor' is struck through and replaced by 'für' above, as the transcription marks.
Line 19: 'persischen Reichs' has a red-ink correction mark at 'Reichs'.
Last line: 'Psammenit' is written as a correction over an earlier name (likely 'Psammis'), with red-ink 'en' added above. The '[?]' can be removed.
